title: Web Workers and CPU-heavy browser work
description: Learn about Web Workers and CPU-heavy browser work. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Web Workers enable JavaScript to run operations in background threads, keeping the main thread free for user interactions. This is essential for CPU-intensive tasks like data processing, image manipulation, and complex calculations that would otherwise block the UI.

JavaScript is single-threaded, meaning all code runs on the main thread. CPU-intensive operations block this thread, causing UI freezing, janky animations, and unresponsive user interactions. Web Workers solve this by providing true multi-threading capabilities.

data.text: Web Workers run in separate threads with their own memory space. They communicate with the main thread via message passing, enabling parallel processing without blocking the UI.

items: No DOM access - workers cannot manipulate the DOM
No window object - limited to self and worker APIs
Same-origin policy - workers must be from same domain
Communication overhead - message passing has performance cost
Not suitable for all tasks - small computations may not benefit

data.text: For small projects or prototypes, you can create inline workers using Blob URLs. This avoids separate worker files but is less maintainable for production code.

data.text: Integrating Web Workers with React requires careful lifecycle management. Workers should be created in useEffect and cleaned up to prevent memory leaks.

data.title: React Worker Hook

data.text: Efficient communication between main thread and workers is crucial. Use structured cloning for complex data, transferables for large buffers, and batch operations to minimize communication overhead.

data.content: Efficiently transfer large data with zero-copy.

data.text: For multiple parallel tasks, use a worker pool to manage worker lifecycles and balance load across available workers.

data.title: Worker Overhead
data.text: Workers have creation and communication overhead. Use them for CPU-intensive tasks (50ms+), not for simple operations. Measure performance to ensure workers actually improve your specific use case.
Modern alternatives to traditional Web Workers include OffscreenCanvas for rendering, Worklets for specialized tasks, and browser-native APIs for specific use cases.

terms.definition: JavaScript API that enables running scripts in background threads, separate from the main thread.
The primary browser thread where UI rendering and user interactions occur.
Objects that can be transferred between workers and main thread with zero-copy, improving performance for large data transfers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Web Workers enable parallel processing to keep the main thread responsive
Use workers for CPU-intensive tasks (50ms+ computation time)
Workers cannot access DOM - communicate via message passing
Clean up workers properly to prevent memory leaks
Use transferable objects for efficient large data transfers
Consider worker pools for multiple parallel tasks
Measure performance to ensure workers provide actual benefit
React requires careful worker lifecycle management with useEffect
data.takeaway: Web Workers are essential for maintaining responsive UIs during CPU-intensive operations, but require careful implementation and performance measurement.
